title: Quarantine flaky CI tests and attribute failures to ticket scope
goal: CI failures unrelated to a ticket change keep burning full 15+ minute verification cycles and fallback routing. Case study: ticket b1c069e0-1875-4aa7-b51d-4c4399b2be31 (binary-safe proof artifacts and repo-root scratch hygiene) passed all of its own gates but failed automated testing three times on pre-existing flakes: install-runner-wrapper tests asserting on HOME/sandbox install paths, a desktop-1280px header visual snapshot timing out on font settling, and a git serialization test hanging for the full 900s timeout while 7185 other tests passed. Build a small structural fix: (1) a quarantine mechanism for known-flaky tests (tagged, retried, or run in a separate non-blocking lane with a recorded baseline, so one flake cannot fail the whole gate); (2) failure attribution that tells the agent whether a failure is in files the ticket touched versus unrelated suites, so agents stop doing manual pre-existing-ness archaeology. Include the three flaky tests above as the first quarantine entries, keep the ticket-scoped checks blocking, and document how to add or remove entries. Success: a ticket whose own tests pass gets a green scoped signal even when a quarantined suite flakes, and the CI report names which lane failed.
